statement: For each i, let s_i = (positions[i][0], positions[i][1]). Define the reachable set M_i subset of {1,...,8}^2 as follows: if pieces[i] is the ASCII byte sequence for "rook", M_i = { (r,c) in {1,...,8}^2 : r = s_i.0 or c = s_i.1 }; if pieces[i] is "queen", M_i = { (r,c) in {1,...,8}^2 : r = s_i.0 or c = s_i.1 or |r - s_i.0| = |c - s_i.1| }; if pieces[i] is "bishop", M_i = { (r,c) in {1,...,8}^2 : |r - s_i.0| = |c - s_i.1| }. A move combination is a tuple (d_0,...,d_{n-1}) with d_i in M_i for each i. For each i and integer t >= 0, define p_i(t) as follows. Let delta_i = max(|d_i.0 - s_i.0|, |d_i.1 - s_i.1|). If delta_i = 0, then p_i(t) = s_i for all t. If delta_i > 0, let u_i = ((d_i.0 - s_i.0)/delta_i, (d_i.1 - s_i.1)/delta_i); if t >= delta_i then p_i(t) = d_i, and if t < delta_i then p_i(t) = (s_i.0 + t * u_i.0, s_i.1 + t * u_i.1). Because d_i is in M_i, the non-zero entries of u_i are 0 or +/-1 and the path is along an allowed rook/queen/bishop line. A move combination is valid iff for every integer t >= 0 and every pair i != j, p_i(t) != p_j(t). The function returns a result res and res is the number of valid move combinations. Pieces do not block one another; reachability is determined only by the geometric rule above.
preconditions: n = len(pieces) = len(positions); 1 <= n <= 4; for each i with 0 <= i < n, pieces[i] is the ASCII byte sequence for one of "rook", "queen", "bishop"; at most one pieces[i] is "queen"; positions[i] is a vector of length 2 with positions[i][0] and positions[i][1] in {1,2,...,8}; all positions[i] are pairwise distinct.

statement: Let f be any symmetry of the 8x8 board, i.e., a composition of the reflections (r,c) -> (9-r,c) and (r,c) -> (r,9-c) and the transpose (r,c) -> (c,r). Let positions' be obtained from positions by applying f to each position: positions'[i] = [f(positions[i][0], positions[i][1])]. The function returns a result res for (pieces, positions) and a result res' for (pieces, positions'), and res = res'.

statement: The function returns a result res' for (pieces', positions') and a result res for (pieces, positions), and res' = res * |M_new|.
preconditions: Let (pieces, positions) be any input satisfying the constraints with n pieces and n < 4. Let T be a piece type in {"rook", "queen", "bishop"} and P a position in [1,8]^2 such that: (a) if T = "queen", then no piece in pieces is "queen"; (b) P is distinct from all positions in positions; (c) the reachable set M_new of a piece of type T starting at P is disjoint from M_i for every i = 0..n-1, where M_i is the reachable set of piece i. Let pieces' = pieces concatenated with [T] and positions' = positions concatenated with [P].
